Accounts

Add account

Maillet reads mail through Microsoft Graph with your own app registration – see . Whether you may allow it yourself is decided by your organisation: if Microsoft asks for admin approval, it is not allowed without your IT.
Proton Mail Bridge: server 127.0.0.1, port 1143, STARTTLS, accept self-signed certificate, and the bridge password shown in the Bridge app. Codes arrive up to ~40 s late – the Bridge polls Proton only every 20–40 s.

Tag

Rules are assigned to this account by its tag. It stays the same when the account is renamed; renaming it here moves all its rules along.

One-Time Passwords

Preconfigured rules for common services, loaded from the Maillet catalog on GitHub. + adds the rules of the selected language for all accounts, ▾ lets you pick accounts. They then appear under Rules.

One-Time Passwords

Local HTTP endpoint to show codes and links from outside, e.g. from a Tampermonkey script. Listens on 127.0.0.1 only; every request needs the token.

Only links starting with one of these are shown, e.g. https://claude.ai/magic-link. Empty list = any https:// link is accepted.

Endpoints

Code
POST /api/otp/code {"code": "…", "ruleName": "…"}
Link
POST /api/otp/link {"link": "…", "ruleName": "…"}

General

  

    
Language

    
Language of all Maillet windows, the tray menu and notifications.

  

  

    
Open as

      

    

    
Side
      

  

  

    
Inbox

       days
      

    
The inbox view shows the mails of the last days; older ones are loaded on request.

  

  

    
Global shortcut

    
Opens Maillet from anywhere and closes it again, in the form chosen under “Open as”. Click the field and press the keys you want; Backspace clears, Esc cancels.

    

      
      
      
      
    

    

    
Works on X11 desktops (Cinnamon, KDE, XFCE). On Wayland most desktops do not allow global shortcuts.

  







  
Theme

  
Colour theme and style of all Maillet windows, the same choice as in every be spex app. A click applies it at once.

  






  
Actions

  

    
Quick actions

    
What mails offer on hover and when reading. Exits take the mail out of the inbox and sit along the top of a card, marks keep it there and sit on the right. Keep your inbox empty? Turn off “Read / unread”.

    

    
Exits

    

    
Marks

    

    
At most 4 exits and 3 marks fit on a card; more go behind “⋯”. Done always sits in the corner.

  

  

    
Reading

    
    
Off: a mail stays unread – and in the overview – until you mark it as read with the eye or move it on (Done, File, Task).

  

  

    
Categories

    
Targets of “File”. The order sets the keys 1–9. A new folder is created on the server on first use; you can also pick an existing one.

    

    
    
  







  
Notifications

  

    
    
Newsletters, bulk mail and login codes never notify. A click on the notification opens the mail; a burst of mails is collapsed into one notification.

    
    
Otherwise all unread mails count, including newsletters.

  







  
Log

  

    
    
    
    
    
  

  

  
Kept in memory only (last 500 entries), never written to disk. Mail text is not stored; codes are masked – click to reveal. Links are cut after their path.
